text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- The CDU and the opposition SPD discuss a consensus on energy policy
- The coalition has apparently agreed on the financing of Eurofighter 2000, according to German weekend press reports
- Row over whether some property should still be defined as "People's Property" -- effectively state property -- as it was in former East Germany continues
- German President Roman Herzog said Germany should concentrate on its top products and urged the country to push for a stronger position in the global economy
- German farmers could face penalties if they continue to overproduce milk
HANDELSBLATT

- Brandenburg state's premier Manfred Stolpe argues that the gradual abolition of the solidarity tax surcharge, which helps to finance reconstruction in eastern Germany, should take place once the economy in eastern Germany starts to improve
- The cold weather in Europe pushes up heating oil prices
- Airbus is due very soon to undergo restructuring
- The relocation of businesses and jobs abroad is haunting Germany. German firms are investing more abroad than foreigners companies do in Germany. Germany as an industrial location is lacking
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Not published due to public holiday in Bavaria
DIE WELT
- Yeltsin dampens Kohl's optimism. Moscow sticks to its rejection of NATO's expansion in eastern and central Europe

- Senior SPD politician Gerhard Schroeder says he will not submit to a "ban on talking about the euro", saying his reservations about its introduction in Germany were justified and should be expressed openly
- European banks increase their market share of credit business as opposed to their competitors in North America and Japan
CDU and SPD looking for consensus over energy policy
